approach: The area of the triangular v-t graph, and so the average velocity, depends only on the base and height, not on where the peak sits along the base.

steps.text: The distance travelled from 0 to t₀ is the area of the triangle formed by the v-t graph.
steps.equation: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × t₀ × v₀

steps.text: This area formula holds no matter where along the base the peak occurs, so it depends only on t₀ and v₀, and t₀ cancels when finding average velocity.
steps.equation: Average velocity = Area / t₀ = (½ t₀ v₀) / t₀ = v₀/2

steps.text: The average velocity is v₀/2, which depends only on v₀ and not on t₀, so both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason directly gives the result stated in the Assertion.
steps.equation: Assertion true, Reason true, Reason explains Assertion

final_answer.value: If both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is correct explanation of the Assertion.

common_mistakes.text: Assuming the average velocity formula v₀/2 only works when the peak is at the midpoint of t₀, and marking the Reason false for a graph where the peak is off-centre.
